title: Suggestions Required- Best Udemy courses around AI for Game developers, Artists and QA testers
author: Silly_Newt4788
selftext:
Hi folks, 

Our company is laying foundations to bring AI practices across different functions. Need suggestions around which courses of Udemy can be given as reference for up skill. 

Thanks in advance!

comments.author: Defiant_Medicine_823
comments.body: Start a conversation with AI and ask questions until you're an expert.

replies.author: Silly_Newt4788
replies.body: I don’t think that is the right approach here. We would want the approach to be structured, where they don’t rely on AI from the get go. We want them to understand the AI flow can enhance their work - so that their foundations remain intact.

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body:
You're asking good questions that I don't have answers to. Hopefully someone with experience implementing a program like this in a professional environment chimes in.

AI in game dev sentiment in most communities is so bad right now, companies aren't going to openly talk about it, unfortunately. Not the way "regular" software companies are comfortable blogging about it, anyway.

replies.author: Silly_Newt4788
replies.body: I agree. AI is randomly being used anywhere and everywhere. I am all in for the technology as a tool to assist a game dev, but i see folks without the basics of C++ shipping games like it’s no body’s business - and when things break they cannot fix it on their own - even the basic fixes.

replies.author: gefahr
replies.body: Yeah, that's not unique to game dev. I work in B2B tech, on a SaaS. What I see is good engineers going faster, and bad engineers spreading their badness faster. Force multiplier for good or bad.

replies.author: Defiant_Medicine_823
replies.body: You can literally use what you told me as a prompt and get those results.

replies.author: Kadse1337
replies.body:
tbh I don't think that Udemy is the right place to learn using AI for Coding. 

The whole AI-Coding field is far too fast-moving still, and the people that are in the weeds doing actual work with AI Agents and improving their workflows, aren't on Udemy creating courses (which will be outdated again after a month). 

A rather peer-based knowledge-exchange and learning-by-doing approach probably works better imo.

replies.author: Silly_Newt4788
replies.body: The challenge here is the dev team has only 2-3 Sr devs and the rest have 1-1.5yrs. While the intent is there to upskill - in corporates it has to be drilled down from high above.

comments.author: Retronitsu
comments.body:
So you want a course that teaches you how to use AI for game dev etc?
Doesn't AI already give you steps on what to do? Do you really need a tutorial for that?

Your artists must be really happy to see AI integrated onto their workflow.

replies.author: Silly_Newt4788
replies.body: Yeah - for example, how to be good at promt engineering, how to build the first basic MVP using AI workflows. The company has unlimited access to Udemy. Was wondering of any of you have taken any course and can recommend

replies.author: Retronitsu
replies.body: I can't take you seriously at all lol
